ops.text: Hardware decoders built for this purpose already trade some accuracy for speed: the FPGA-based Sandpiper decoder, for example, attains a threshold of $0.672\%$ on the rotated surface code under uniform circuit-level depolarizing noise [⟦new.A10⟧].

Already at $\eta=1$ the correlated model therefore pushes the rotated code below the uncorrelated circuit-level threshold of real-time hardware decoders such as Sandpiper [⟦new.A10⟧], even though MWPF, unlike those decoders, processes the hyperedges natively.

new_bib.text: T. Ashworth, H. Pryce, K. Doyle, A. Rao, and C. Holroyd (2026). Sandpiper: sliding-window cluster matching for real-time surface-code decoding on FPGAs. arXiv e-prints.
